headlines.title: Worried about being shortchanged at the gas pump? Here's what to look for
headlines.description: Have you ever wondered if a gas pump is actually delivering what you’re paying for? It’s a question many people across the country are asking as high prices persist. In the South Bay, the task of checking fuel pump accuracy falls on Santa Clara County’s Weights and Measures Division. “We’re out there every day making sure the customers can feel confident in the gas that they’re buying,” said Ryan Atwood with the Weights and Measures Division. When filling up, consumers should keep an eye out for a seal on the pump that indicates it passed inspection. A pump that pumps too much gas favors customers, but still gets a blue tag, meaning repairs should be made within 30 days. A red tag means the pump is not pouring enough gas and is immediately shut down. What the county doesn’t want to see is people testing the accuracy of a gas pump themselves. The county said that dangerous task should be left to the professionals. “I’m assuring them that if they see one of our seals at the pump, they can be assured that that pump is accurate,” Atwood said. oil and gas Sep 22 oil and gas Sep 17

headlines.title: How the 49ers play into this year's Santa Clara mayoral race
headlines.description: The San Francisco 49ers find themselves in the midst of the hotly contested race for mayor of Santa Clara, the city the team calls home. Santa Clara does not have a primary election for mayor, so all six candidates are on the ballot in November. The 49er influence on voters, whether positive or negative, matters significantly. Supporters of mayoral candidate and former city councilmember Kathy Watanabe gathered near Levi’s Stadium Thursday to cheer her call for an independent audit of how much the 49ers and Levi’s Stadium pay into the city’s general fund, especially from recent big events, such as the Super Bowl and World Cup matches. Their complaints echoed a civil grand jury report a couple years ago that recommended Santa Clara conduct its own economic impact analysis. “When a public asset generates private revenue and profits, the public deserves transparency,” Watanabe said. “This shouldn’t be about being pro-49ers or even anti-49ers. It should be about being pro-Santa Clara.” The 49ers emphatically counter that they are a good partner with Santa Clara and transparent in their financial payments to the city. The franchise offered a list of local businesses that they say benefit from the 49ers and Levi’s Stadium. The 49ers, citing public records, said stadium revenue has generated more than $30 million to Santa Clara’s general fund in the past two years and said “Ms. Watanabe is either misinformed or intentionally misleading the public.” David Kertes, another mayoral candidate, said audits are nice but not enough and blamed city leadership for any lack of transparency with the 49ers. In a statement, the city said, so far, it has received about 95% of the reimbursement it expected to get from the 49ers and confirmed the city made about $3 million from Super Bowl hotel tax revenue. All of the mayoral candidates will get a chance to address the issues at a debate this Sunday.

headlines.title: Activists rally after incident involving day laborers at Concord Home Depot
headlines.description: Pro-immigration groups gathered outside Home Depot in Concord on Thursday to protest what they say was the detention of four day laborers. They believe federal agents were involved, but the two most likely agencies said they weren’t. The Concord Immigrants Protections Network said a witness gave one of its volunteers a video showing what appeared to be federal agents detaining four day laborers at a Home Depot parking lot. “He was able to speak to witnesses who told him that four day laborers were taken into these unmarked SUVs,” Tony Bravo with the Concord Immigrant Protections Network said. However, NBC Bay Area’s sister station Telemundo 48 contacted ICE and CBP, and the agencies said they weren’t the ones that made the arrests. Activists say what happened is causing some panic, regardless of which agency was involved. In a statement, Home Depot said in part, “We aren’t notified that immigration enforcement activities are going to happen, and we aren’t involved in the operations. We aren’t coordinating with ICE or Border Patrol. We cannot legally interfere with federal enforcement agencies.” Activists said they don’t have any information on who the detainees are.

headlines.title: Elizabeth Holmes to be transferred to a halfway house
headlines.description: Elizabeth Holmes, who was convicted of fraud for siphoning hundreds of millions of dollars from several high-profile investors, is scheduled to be transferred from a minimum-security federal prison to a halfway house next year, according to one of her victims. Holmes, 42, defrauded investors of millions through Theranos, the failed blood-testing company that she founded. She was sentenced in 2022 to 11 years and three months in prison. She and her business partner Ramesh “Sunny” Balwani were ordered to pay 12 victims a total of $452 million in restitution. Holmes has been serving that sentence at a minimum-security prison in Bryan, Texas. The halfway house will provide her greater freedom. Alan Eisenman, one of her victims, said she is to be transferred to the Austin Transitional Center, a halfway house in Del Valle, an unincorporated community that borders Austin, Texas. The Department of Justice is required by law to notify victims of crime of case developments through letters and emails. Scott Taylor, a spokesperson for the Bureau of Prisons, said he could not provide details of Holmes’ confinement, including release plans. Taylor cited safety, security and a Bureau of Prisons policy that says such information can’t be released until after an individual arrives at their designated institution. Movies Sep 7 Elizabeth Holmes Jul 11, 2023 Eisenman, an early Theranos investor who testified at Holmes’ trial, said he received a message from the Justice Department’s victim notification system Wednesday saying the halfway house transfer would occur in August 2027. Eisenman, a retired financial planner from Texas, invested about $1.2 million with his family in the failed blood-testing company beginning in 2006. He was the smallest investor among a list of high-profile, well-monied investors who included Australian media mogul Rupert Murdoch. Eisenman was unhappy to hear of the planned transfer. “Seems like a gift,” he told NBC News. Holmes owes Eisenman and his wife, Sherrie, almost $150,000 out of a total of $452 million in restitution for all victims of her crimes, according to a court document. So far, he has “not received a penny” from Holmves, he told NBC News. “She was a liar back in 2006,” Eisenman said, “and she’s a liar today.” Eisenman said he hoped Holmes would remain in prison through her scheduled release date of Feb. 22, 2030, after some reductions in the sentence. In March, a judge cut Holmes’ sentence from 135 months to 123 months. According to a court document, the judge agreed with Holmes that she did not personally cause “substantial financial hardship” to her victims. The government had tried to prevent a reduction of her prison time, arguing that Holmes has not accepted responsibility for her crimes, paid minimal restitution and “has the opportunity to reoffend,” according to a court filing. The government told the court that Holmes has continued to tell national media she intends to resume a career in healthcare technology after her release and has been advising her romantic partner on fundraising for his startup, a company that has similarities to Theranos, the court document states. Eisenman added that he’s against Holmes receiving any form of presidential clemency. She filed for a commutation of her sentence last year. It remains pending. Holmes’ attorney from her trial did not respond to a phone message from NBC News requesting comment. ABC News first reported her pending release to the halfway house. Walter Pavlo, president of Prisonology LLC consulting firm, said a combination of factors could have helped reduce the time Holmes is spending in prison and at the halfway house. Those include a change on sentencing guidelines, good conduct time, possible participation in programs that slice time off her sentence if successfully completed and laws governing time she would spend in a halfway house and home confinement. Pavlo said inmates who report to halfway houses can work, have a phone and drive to religious services or shop for things they need and can earn passes for weekends at home. On its website, the Bureau of Prisons states that inmates at halfway houses are given counseling, job placement and other programs and services to help rebuild community ties. The BOP site states it monitors inmates’ activities, requires sign out and conducts head counts. Also, inmates “ordinarily” are expected to work 40 hours a week within 15 days of their arrival at the halfway house and some of their income pay for some of their stay at the halfway house, according to the BOP site. The news of Holmes’ impending move comes as a documentary about her is about to be released. The documentary by comedian Nathan Fielder and director Lance Oppenheim is based on Fielder living with her and her partner for several days before she entered prison in 2023. It recently made its debut at the Telluride Film Festival and is scheduled for full release next month. Eisenman said he also watched the latest trailer for the documentary, “You Can See Everything,” and plans to see it upon its release next month. His concern, he added, is whether it will portray Holmes as a sympathetic figure. “She’s obviously manipulative,” Eisenman said. “If people don’t see that, then they’re blind. She’s the most conniving person I’ve ever met.”
headlines.source: Suzanne Gamboa and Erik Ortiz | NBC News

headlines.title: San Jose restaurant owner frustrated by frequent break-ins
headlines.description: A San Jose restaurant owner who said she has lost count of how many times burglars have struck her business is calling on the city to do more. The owner of Mendoza’s Restaurant, located on McKee Road near Regional Medical Center, walked into work Wednesday morning to find broken glass. The owner said this time the burglars did not take anything because there was nothing of value. The owner is tired of the constant break-ins and the costs that come with repairing broken glass and equipment. She reports the break-ins to police and said officers come by to ask questions and take pictures, but she said she never hears of any arrests. headlines.title: Walmart settles for $16 million over expired goods on California shelves
headlines.description: Walmart Inc. has agreed to settle a civil lawsuit brought by seven California counties for $16 million over allegedly keeping baby formula and medication on shelves past their expiration dates, the Solano County District Attorney’s Office said Wednesday. The suit, brought by Solano, Alameda, Sacramento, San Bernardino, San Joaquin, Sonoma and Yolo counties, found that the retail giant routinely sold expired products, including cough syrup, sunscreen and cosmetics. An investigation found no evidence anyone was physically harmed by the expired goods. Walmart was cooperative during the investigation, according to the district attorney’s office. “Parents should never have to worry that the infant formula or medications they purchase for their children are expired and potentially unsafe,” said Solano County District Attorney Krishna Abrams. The settlement “strengthens safeguards to prevent similar violations in the future,” Abrams said. As part of the settlement, Walmart is prohibited from selling baby formula and over the counter drugs past the use date in all California stores. The company was also ordered to implement a training program for employees to better identify expired goods and take them off shelves. Walmart will also pay over $15.7 million in penalties and $250,000 in fees.

headlines.title: Motorcyclist killed in collision with turning vehicle in Fremont
headlines.description: A man riding a motorcycle in Fremont Wednesday died after colliding with a vehicle that was making a turn in an intersection. The collision happened at about 1:40 p.m. at Hastings and Keats streets, the Fremont Police Department said in a statement. The motorcyclist was riding northbound on Hastings Street and was traveling through the intersection when he collided with a passenger vehicle that was making a left turn from Keats Street onto southbound Hastings Street, according to a preliminary investigation by the police department’s traffic unit. The motorcyclist was unresponsive when police and paramedics arrived. He was pronounced dead from his injuries at a local hospital. It marked the 10th fatal traffic collision in Fremont in 2026, according to the police department. The collision remained under investigation Wednesday. Anyone with information was asked to contact the Fremont Police Department Traffic Unit at 510-790-6760.

headlines.title: Crews remove derelict boats from Oakland Estuary
headlines.description: Crews on Thursday spent time removing derelict boats from the Oakland Estuary as part of a massive cleanup effort. Officials said over the next two weeks marine units will remove more than a dozen sunken vessels from the waterway. “So far this year more than 50 abandoned vessels, derelict or surrendered, were removed from this estuary,” Oakland police Chief James Beere said. “A year ago we came out here and there were boats dumped on the dry dock, in the parking lot, with masts coming out from the top of the water.” NBC Bay Area’s Christie Smith has more on the cleanup effort in the video report above.

headlines.title: Steph Curry visits East Oakland school, talks vision issue
headlines.description: Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry visited Madison Park Academy Primary in East Oakland on Wednesday to discuss a personal health issue. Curry is battling the progressive eye condition keratoconus, which effects vision. He didn’t let the serious topic dampen the day, joining the students for a book distribution and basketball clinic, while sharing his personal mission to inspire children to overcome physical obstacles. Curry said the diagnosis caused him anxiety, but he’s learned to manage it. Steph Curry 23 hours ago Steph Curry Sep 23 Steph Curry reveals rare eye condition diagnosis during Warriors' dynasty run

headlines.title: Authorities search for missing person in the water in Antioch
headlines.description: Authorities said they are searching for a missing person in the water in Antioch Wednesday. Contra Costa Fire said they were dispatched to a report of a person in the water at around 6:16 p.m. at 1 Marina Plz in Antioch. Crews arrived on boats and rescued one person, who was then taken to the hospital with non-life-threatening injuries. Authorities said there were reports of another person still in the water. Just before 10:30 p.m., the Coast Guard confirmed to NBC Bay Area the search is ongoing for the missing person.

headlines.title: Man struck, killed by vehicle in Richmond
headlines.description: A 65-year-old man was killed after being stuck by a vehicle in Richmond on Thursday morning, according to police. Richmond police officers responded to the 2300 block of Maricopa Avenue following a fatal collision involving a vehicle and a pedestrian. The victim, a Richmond resident, was out for his morning walk, according to his family. The driver remained at the scene and cooperated with investigators, police said. Maricopa Avenue was closed between 23rd and 24th streets while officers investigated. Drivers were asked to avoid the area and use alternate routes. Additional information was not immediately available.

headlines.title: BART considers adding more surveillance cameras as part of safety push
headlines.description: BART leaders are looking at the impact of surveillance cameras across the transit system, with the possibility of adding more. BART officials say surveillance cameras, along with the agency’s new fare gates, have been instrumental in cutting down on crime. BART will ask its board to continue the surveillance already in place and add two new cameras — one at BART Police Department headquarters and another at the Union City at-grade pedestrian crossing. Closed-circuit television cameras are used extensively across BART to identify and prevent threats to people and property. According to BART, the cameras assisted with more than 3,700 video requests. More than 2,300 were for criminal investigations, more than 1,300 were for train car video and more than two dozen were for court subpoenas. BART police also produced 220 wanted-person bulletins using images from the cameras. The data comes as BART marks one year since new fare gates were installed at all 50 stations. BART says crime against riders has dropped 67%, while safety delays have been cut by nearly half. Officials also estimate the new gates have brought in roughly $10 million that would have otherwise been lost to fare evasion. BART riders surveyed say they are satisfied with the transit agency. The data comes as transit agencies, including BART, face a financial cliff. Voters are being asked to approve two ballot measures in November as BART faces a roughly $300 million budget deficit.
